standard.title: Intertextual references in visual texts
standard.description: investigate how visual texts use intertextual references to enhance and layer meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can understand how images and visual elements create meaning and position viewers (AC9E7LA07). They have not yet examined how visual texts deliberately reference other texts — in the form of intertextuality — to create additional layers of meaning that depend on a viewer's prior cultural knowledge.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can investigate how visual texts use intertextual references to enhance and layer meaning, including how words and images interact in the creation of intertextual meaning.

nodes.label: What intertextuality is in visual texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify an intertextual reference in a visual text and explain that its meaning depends on a viewer's knowledge of the original source text.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one intertextual reference in a provided visual text (e.g. an advertisement or image) and explain what source text or cultural knowledge it draws on.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain intertextual references in advertisements, images or other visual texts; explain how these references depend on viewer knowledge and what effect is created for viewers who recognise vs do not recognise the reference.
wider: Compare two visual texts that reference the same source text (e.g. two advertisements referencing the same cultural icon) and analyse how the same reference can be used to different effects
Investigate how visual parody relies on intertextual recognition — how the comedy or critique only works if the viewer knows the source
Examine how visual texts from different cultural contexts use intertextual references to cultural materials that may not translate across audiences

response_modes.reason: The concept that intertextual meaning is audience-dependent (not intrinsic to the image) can be abstract. Seeing examples where some students get the reference and others don't — or comparing references that span cultural contexts — makes this contingency concrete.

success_criteria: Identifies a specific intertextual reference in a visual text and names the source it draws on.
Explains how a viewer's recognition of the source text affects the meaning they make from the visual text.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to explain how intertextual references layer meaning — a task that depends on understanding that meaning is audience-dependent (requires prior knowledge of the source). Students who arrive at Node 2 still treating textual meaning as intrinsic to the image will produce surface-level description rather than intertextual analysis.

nodes.label: How intertextual references layer meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how intertextual references in visual texts enhance and layer meaning — particularly how the interrelationship of words and images in advertisements creates layered meaning through cultural allusion.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate how one advertisement uses a combination of words and images to create a layered intertextual meaning — identifying what the reference adds that a literal reading of the text would not contain.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how visual texts including advertisements use intertextual references — through images, words or their interrelationship — to enhance meaning by activating cultural associations that go beyond what is literally depicted or written.
wider: Analyse how a series of advertisements from one brand use a consistent intertextual strategy to build cumulative cultural associations over time
Investigate how intertextual references in visual art (e.g. contemporary painting or photography referencing historical artworks) create dialogue between past and present
Create a visual text that deliberately uses an intertextual reference to layer meaning, then explain the choices made and the effect intended

response_modes.reason: The breadth of intertextual strategies across visual media — advertising, art, meme culture, film — helps students see that intertextuality is a pervasive feature of contemporary visual communication, not confined to one text type.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Advertising and contemporary visual culture offer abundant high-engagement examples of intertextuality that students bring cultural knowledge to. Investigating how commercial and artistic contexts deploy intertextuality differently is genuinely rich comparative territory.
success_criteria: Explains how the intertextual reference in a visual text adds layers of meaning beyond the literal content.
Analyses the interrelationship of words and images in a visual text to show how they work together to create the intertextual effect.
